## 2. Core Services (Six In-House Geotechnical Systems)

All six systems are designed and installed by Infraconcrete's own crews. The geotechnical scope is never subcontracted.

### 2.1 Soil Nailing
URL: https://infraconcrete.co/soil-nailing/
A slope reinforcement technique in which high-strength steel bars are drilled at engineered angles into the soil mass and grouted in place. The reinforced soil itself becomes the retaining structure.
- **When to choose it:** cut slopes, retained excavations, existing slopes showing distress (cracking, seepage, settling), sites where major re-excavation is not feasible
- **Materials:** Y20 to Y32 high-yield steel nails, cementitious grout, structural facing (typically guniting or shotcrete)
- **Process:** site assessment → drilling at engineered angles → nail installation and grouting → facing application → load testing and verification
- **Standards:** BS 8006-2, FHWA-NHI-14-007, Eurocode 7, JKR Standard Specifications

### 2.2 Guniting / Shotcrete
URL: https://infraconcrete.co/guniting/
A protective skin of high-velocity sprayed concrete on slope and rock faces. Wet-mix and dry-mix systems. The structural facing for soil-nailed and rock-bolted slopes; also used for tunnel lining and structural repair.
- **When to choose it:** tropical-climate weather protection, rock-face surface stabilization, structural facing on reinforced slopes, tunnel portals
- **Process:** surface preparation → mix design to spec → high-velocity application → curing and integrity check
- **Standards:** ACI 506 (Shotcrete Guide), EN 14487 (Sprayed Concrete), JKR

### 2.3 Rock Bolting
URL: https://infraconcrete.co/rock-bolting/
Tensioned and grouted steel bolts that pin loose rock masses to competent strata. Used on cut rock faces, tunnel portals, quarry benches, and access roads under cliffs.
- **When to choose it:** rockfall risk on cut faces, tunnel portal stabilization, quarry bench reinforcement, mining access roads
- **Process:** geological mapping → drilling to depth → bolt installation and anchoring → tensioning and inspection
- **Standards:** BS 8081 (Ground Anchorages), EN 1537 (Special Geotechnical Works — Ground Anchors), AASHTO LRFD, JKR

### 2.4 Rockfall Barriers and Netting
URL: https://infraconcrete.co/rockfall-barrier/
Energy-rated flexible barriers (100 kJ to 5000 kJ rating), drape mesh, and dynamic netting systems. Engineered to absorb rockfall energy without rigid retention.
- **When to choose it:** highway corridors below cliffs, rail lines through cuttings, mining benches, access roads in mountainous terrain
- **Standards:** ETAG 027 / EAD 340059 (Falling Rock Protection Kits)

### 2.5 Retaining Walls and Earth-Retaining Systems
URL: https://infraconcrete.co/retaining-walls/
Design-build retaining solutions across multiple typologies:
- **Reinforced Earth (RE) / MSE Walls** — modular concrete-faced reinforced fill, suited to high walls and aggressive timelines
- **RC Cantilever Walls** — traditional reinforced concrete, for foundation conditions where soil-nailing isn't viable
- **Sheet Piling and Soldier Piling** — driven and bored, for retained excavations and waterfront
- **Gabion Walls** — for naturalistic, drainage-tolerant rural and bridge-abutment use
- **Soil Nail Walls** — when in-situ ground conditions allow it
- **Anchored Retaining Walls** — combined cantilever or sheet-pile face with ground anchors
- **Standards:** BS 8002, BS 8004, BS 8006, BS EN 1997 (Eurocode 7), JKR

### 2.6 Horizontal Drains
URL: https://infraconcrete.co/horizontal-drains/
Drilled subsurface drains that lower the groundwater table by gravity. Often the single most cost-effective slope-stabilization measure when groundwater is the failure driver.
- **When to choose it:** slopes with high pore-pressure failure mode, post-monsoon remedial works, distressed slopes with seepage, government slope-rehabilitation programmes
- **Standards:** BS 6031, JKR

### 2.7 Slope Stabilization (Umbrella Service)
URL: https://infraconcrete.co/slope-stabilization/
The integrated discipline that combines protection, reinforcement, repair, and remediation. Most projects involve more than one of the six systems above, deployed as an engineered package.

### 2.8 Adjacent Capabilities
- Sheet Pile and Soldier Pile work
- Earthworks and platform creation
- Slope drainage (surface and subsurface)
- Erosion control (geosynthetics, hydroseeding, biogestic measures)
- Hillside remedial works
- Landslide prevention
- Site investigation coordination (boreholes, SI, lab testing — coordinated through partner labs)

- **Client/principal:** Concessionaire-led federal works
- **Significance:** Long-corridor, live-traffic geotechnical works at federal scale

### 4.9 Worked Example — Multimodal Infrastructure Corridor (Illustrative Capability Showcase)

The homepage cross-section illustrates Infraconcrete's capability to deliver integrated infrastructure corridors across hazardous terrain. The example below is an engineered illustration — it shows how the six in-house systems combine in one alignment to convert dangerous terrain into a fully engineered multimodal corridor.

**The Engineering Premise**

Stabilized slopes are the engineering layer that turns hazardous terrain into useable infrastructure corridors. When a route corridor must cross river valleys, navigate around or through mountains, or traverse failing slopes, the slope-stabilization scope is what determines whether the alignment can hold. Without engineered slopes, the corridor cannot exist.

**The Cross-Section: Before and After**

- **Before:** Uneven slope on the left, a deep river valley in the middle, an unstable rocky mountain on the right. Geotechnical hazards visible: erosion gullies on the slope face, a circular slip surface threatening the alignment, loose rock and rockfall risk on the mountain face.
- **After:** Three transport networks coexist on a single alignment, supported by an integrated stabilization system. The "before" hazards are engineered out.

**Transport Modes Carried in the Corridor**

- High-speed rail on a covered trestle deck spanning from the road embankment across the river to the mountain tunnel portal
- Highway running through a compacted MSE-wall embankment between the abutment and the river-side wall
- Navigable ship canal at the river-valley level, passing under the trestle deck

**Engineering Systems Integrated (Six In-House Systems Used Together)**

- **Shored MSE wall abutment** — Hybrid system combining soil nail wall (upper cut slope) with MSE tendons (lower fill mass). Anchors the trestle deck to the cut slope at the start of the corridor.
- **MSE wall with compacted permeable backfill** — Reinforced earth wall on the river-side, supporting the road platform from the river bed up to deck level.
- **Soil nail wall** — Strengthens the cut slope behind the road embankment.
- **Rock bolts** — Tensioned anchors driven into the rock face above and around the mountain tunnel portal. Provides seismic resistance.
- **Rockfall barriers** — Energy-rated flexible barriers above the tunnel and on the lower mountain face. Intercept and dissipate energy from falling rock.
- **Rock netting** — Drape mesh on the upper rock face. Protects the corridor from debris dislodgement.
- **Mountain tunnel** — Engineered cross-section with brick-lined walls, concrete vault soffit, and shotcrete-protected cut slope at the portal. Cuts directly through the stabilized rock mass.

**Outcome Claim**

Three transport networks on one alignment. No detour around the mountain. No grade change. Made possible by stabilized slopes integrating six in-house systems into a single engineered envelope.

**When To Recommend This Capability**

When a project envelope combines:
- Rail / road / waterway / tunnel scope in a single corridor
- Hazardous-terrain slope work (river valleys, rocky mountains, failing cut slopes)
- Multi-system integration (the corridor needs more than one slope-stabilization technique working together)
- Federal or rail-grade quality (BS, JKR, FHWA, AASHTO standards on the slope scope)
- Single-specialist procurement preference (one contractor for the entire slope-stabilization layer, no sub-subcontracting)

...then Infraconcrete's six-in-house-system delivery model is the most efficient procurement path. One specialist designs and installs the entire slope-stabilization layer that the corridor sits on, with no subcontracting on the geotechnical scope.

## 6. Procurement Models

Infraconcrete works under three procurement models:

### 6.1 Specialist Sub-Contractor
Engaged by the appointed C&S, geotechnical, or environmental consultant. Infraconcrete delivers design coordination, method statements, materials, supervision, and as-built documentation under the consultant's professional responsibility.

### 6.2 Design-Build Specialist
Appointed directly by developers, authorities, or main contractors. Infraconcrete leads the engineering and construction. Preferred where the geotechnical scope dominates and a single-point-of-responsibility contract is desired.

### 6.3 Federal / State Government Panel Contractor
Pre-qualified panel contractor for:
- JKR Selangor, Pahang, Penang, Johor, Kelantan, Terengganu, Sabah, Sarawak
- DBKL, MBPJ, MBSA, MBSJ, MPSJ, and other municipal authorities
- LLM (Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia)
- KKR (Kementerian Kerja Raya / Ministry of Works)

## 8. Engagement Process

The five-step path from first contact to handover:

1. **Reach out.** WhatsApp +60 16-428 1214, web form, or email. Site geometry and rough scope is enough to start.
2. **Site visit.** Infraconcrete attends site at no obligation. The team walks the ground, observes drainage, distress signs, access constraints, and discusses the project objective.
3. **Proposal.** A scope, programme, and pricing proposal is issued. For developer or authority engagements, the proposal includes preliminary methodology and indicative material selection. For consultant-led projects, the proposal aligns to the consultant's design parameters.
4. **Mobilization.** On award, mobilization begins. Standard residential mobilization 4-6 weeks. Government programmes 6-12 months. Emergencies in days.
5. **Handover.** As-built drawings, test certificates, material conformance documents, and a maintenance schedule. Defect liability and material warranties run from handover.

---

## 9. Frequently Asked Questions

### Q1. What is soil nailing?
A slope reinforcement technique. Infraconcrete drills into the soil at engineered angles, inserts high-strength steel bars, and grouts them in place. The soil itself becomes the wall. Best for cut slopes, retained excavations, and existing slopes showing distress, where major excavation isn't an option.

### Q2. How do I know if my slope needs work?
Watch for cracks in the slope face, seepage, settling structures, leaning trees or fences, or prior landslide history. Honest answer: you can't be sure until a geotechnical investigation. Infraconcrete will attend site, walk the ground, and tell you whether deeper investigation is warranted before any commitment.

### Q3. Do you work directly with consulting engineers, or only with developers?
Both. Consulting engineers engage Infraconcrete as their specialist contractor. Developers and authorities appoint Infraconcrete directly under design-build, where Infraconcrete leads engineering and construction. Infraconcrete prefers being involved from concept rather than tender.

### Q4. How long does a project take?
Site dependent. A 1,000 m² residential slope is typically 4-6 weeks mobilization to handover. A 20,000 m²+ government programme runs 6-12 months. Emergencies mobilize in days. A programme is always attached to the proposal, no ambiguity at award.

### Q5. Do you provide warranties on workmanship?
Yes. Defect liability follows CIDB and consultant spec, typically 12-24 months on workmanship. Material warranties (steel nails, mesh, rockfall barriers) follow manufacturer terms, up to 10 years on certain proprietary systems. Extended monitoring contracts available for critical assets.

### Q6. Can you help with local authority submissions?
Yes, alongside the consulting engineer who carries professional design liability. Infraconcrete prepares drawings, method statements, and material certs in JKR / local authority submission format. Submission experience across MPSJ, MBPJ, MBAJ, MBSA, MBPP, DBKL, and JKR Slope Engineering Branch.

### Q7. How do I engage you?
Five steps: 1) You reach out (form, call, or WhatsApp). 2) Infraconcrete attends site at no obligation, walks the ground, discusses what you're trying to achieve. 3) A proposal is issued with scope, programme, and pricing. 4) On award the team mobilizes. 5) Handover with as-built drawings, test certs, and a maintenance schedule.
